# User Story

As a Working Capital loan operations user (Admin/Customer),
I want backdated repayments to be correctly recorded on their actual transaction date and trigger reprocessing of subsequent transactions when necessary,
So that loan balances, principal allocations, charge allocations, and delinquency tracking remain accurate and consistent regardless of the order in which repayments are recorded.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a customer makes a repayment dated earlier than an already-recorded repayment (backdated repayment), the system must recompute and reflect the correct principal outstanding, total paid principal, and overpayment amount, independent of the order in which repayments were entered.
- When a loan has no charges, principal-only allocation across multiple repayments (including backdated ones) must be order-independent, leaving previously recorded transactions' allocations unchanged.
- When a backdated repayment causes the total repaid amount to exceed the outstanding principal, the excess must be recorded as an overpayment amount, without redistributing the allocation of other transactions.
- When multiple backdated repayments are made in any sequence (including between two existing repayments), the system must accumulate principal outstanding, total paid principal, and transaction records correctly for all repayments.
- When repayments are made sequentially in chronological order (non-backdated), the system must process balances and allocations normally without triggering unnecessary reprocessing side effects.
- When a backdated repayment is made before a charge's due date, the repayment must be allocated as principal-only, while the later repayment made on or after the charge's due date must settle the charge first per the fee-first allocation order.
- When a single repayment covers multiple lapsed delinquency periods, the system must distribute the paid amount across periods based on each period's remaining outstanding balance, correctly updating expected amount, paid amount, outstanding amount, minimum payment criteria met status, delinquent amount, and delinquent days for each period.
- When a backdated repayment is recorded, the projected amortization schedule structure must remain a static, unaffected projection, while the recalculated principal outstanding must reflect the actual impact of the backdated payment.
- When a backdated repayment is made on a loan configured with a breach schedule, the outstanding balance tracked by the breach schedule must be reduced accordingly after the inline COB job processes the loan.
- When a backdated repayment causes a later transaction's fee allocation to no longer apply (because the earlier backdated transaction now claims the fee), the later transaction must be reprocessed to reallocate its portion fully to principal, following the fee-first allocation order defined by the loan product.
- When a repayment is made against a loan with a due fee, the transaction must split allocation between fee and principal according to the product's configured payment allocation order (e.g., fee before principal), and the charge balance (fee amount, fee paid, fee outstanding) must be updated to reflect the settlement.

As a Loan System Administrator,
I want the system to automatically execute the Close of Business (COB) process inline (in real-time) whenever a loan transaction occurs after the business date has advanced beyond the loan's last closed business date,
So that loan statuses, delinquency classifications, and overdue calculations remain accurate and up-to-date even when the scheduled batch COB job has not yet run, without requiring manual intervention.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When the inline COB job is manually triggered for a loan, the system correctly updates the loan's delinquency range and delinquent date based on the elapsed business days since disbursement.
- When the business date advances by multiple days, running the inline COB job should cause the loan to "catch up," setting the last closed business date to one day prior to the current business date.
- When a repayment transaction is made on a loan whose last closed business date is behind the current business date, the inline COB process should trigger automatically (via the loan's ID or external ID) to bring the loan's business date up to date before or as part of processing the transaction.
- If no COB process has ever been applied to a loan before, a repayment transaction (whether identified by loan ID or external ID) should NOT trigger an inline COB job, and the loan's last closed business date should remain "null" after the transaction.
- If a COB process has previously been applied to a loan, a subsequent repayment transaction (whether identified by loan ID or external ID) SHOULD trigger an inline COB job, updating the last closed business date accordingly (to one day prior to the transaction date).
- Even when a loan account is locked by an administrator, a repayment transaction should still trigger the inline COB execution, correctly closing the business date, updating the loan status to "CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET," clearing the outstanding balance, generating the correct journal entries, and recording accurate delinquency history (added/lifted dates).
- The inline COB and delinquency/lock behavior described above must hold true consistently for both default (simple) loan products and advanced/progressive loan products (e.g., those using Advanced Payment Allocation and interest recalculation rules).

As a Loan Administrator,
I want the loan repayment schedule and Interest Refund transactions to be automatically recalculated whenever a repayment or refund transaction is reversed, and post-maturity due date charges to be correctly recognized on the repayment schedule,
So that the loan balances, interest amounts, and outstanding dues remain accurate and consistent regardless of transaction reversals or late-added charges.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a repayment transaction is undone after an Interest Refund has already been processed, the system must recalculate the repayment schedule, correctly reallocate principal and interest across transactions, and mark the original repayment and related transactions as "reverted" while creating replayed counterparts.
- When a Merchant Issued Refund transaction is undone, the system must reverse the associated Interest Refund transaction, recalculate the outstanding schedule with newly accrued interest, and correctly reflect the reverted status on both the Merchant Issued Refund and Interest Refund transactions in the Loan Transactions tab.
- When a due date charge (e.g., NSF fee) is added after the loan's original maturity date, the system must extend the repayment schedule with an additional period reflecting the charge, correctly recalculate the total due/outstanding amounts, and ensure the charge appears properly in the Loan Charges tab whether or not an inline COB job has been run.
- After all recalculations, the loan must still support a full pay-off transaction that results in the "CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET" status once all outstanding principal, interest, fees, and penalties are settled.

As a Financial Administrator,
I want to migrate backdated loans into the system and have the Close of Business (COB) job correctly recalculate schedules, accruals, charges, and delinquency status,
So that historical loan data (with past disbursements, repayments, and charges) is accurately reflected in the system without requiring day-by-day COB execution for every missed business date.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a loan is created, approved, and disbursed with a backdated submission and disbursement date, the repayment schedule must be generated correctly based on the original terms, showing accurate principal, interest, and due amounts for each period.

- Backdated repayments (full or partial) applied after loan migration must correctly update the repayment schedule, transaction history, and outstanding balances, including proper allocation to principal, interest, fees, and penalties.
- Running a single inline COB job after migration must correctly generate all missing accrual entries (both "Accrual Activity" and "Accrual" transactions) for each period up to the current business date, without requiring COB to run for each individual missed day.
- After COB execution, the loan's total overdue amount and delinquency status must be accurately calculated based on all recorded transactions and charges.
- The system must correctly record and expose the "last closed business date" of the loan after each COB execution.
- When the business date advances further and COB is run again, the system must generate only the incremental accrual entries for the new period(s), without duplicating or recalculating previously settled transactions.
- The final repayment schedule, transaction history, and total row summaries must remain consistent and accurate across multiple COB executions following migration.

As a Loan Officer,
I want the system to correctly recalculate the repayment schedule, interest amounts, and accounting entries when a multi-disbursement progressive loan with flat interest receives an additional disbursement at various points in the repayment cycle (mid-period or on the installment due date),
So that I can accurately manage tranche disbursements, ensure correct interest accrual and journal postings, and safely reverse repayments or disbursements when corrections are needed without corrupting the loan's financial data.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a second disbursement is made on a loan with flat interest and multi-disbursement enabled, the repayment schedule must be recalculated to redistribute the additional principal and recompute interest across the remaining installments, regardless of whether the disbursement occurs mid-period or exactly on an installment due date.
- The recalculation behavior must be consistent across different interest calculation conventions (e.g., actual/actual and 360/30), with the schedule reflecting split balance rows for the disbursement date and updated principal, interest, and due amounts for affected installments.
- Each disbursement transaction must generate correct journal entries (debiting Loans Receivable and crediting the Suspense/Clearing account) for the exact disbursed amount, and the Loan Transactions tab must reflect all disbursements with accurate running loan balances.
- When a customer repayment is made via AUTOPAY covering all outstanding dues, the system must correctly allocate the payment across principal and interest for each installment, update paid/in-advance/late/outstanding statuses, and generate an accrual transaction alongside proper repayment journal entries.
- The system must support undoing a repayment and undoing the last disbursement, correctly reverting the loan schedule and transaction history back to the state prior to those actions, with reverted transactions clearly flagged (Reverted = true) while preserving the integrity of prior transactions (Replayed = false).

As a Loan Officer,
I want to apply an Interest Payment Waiver transaction on a loan account with different payment allocation strategies, timings, and amounts,
So that I can waive part or all of the interest due for a borrower while accurately reflecting the impact on the repayment schedule, transaction history, and accounting journal entries.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The system must allow an Interest Payment Waiver transaction to be applied on the due date, before the due date, or after the maturity date, with either the exact outstanding interest amount or a partial amount.
- When the waiver amount exceeds the interest due, the system must correctly allocate the remaining amount to principal, fees, or penalties based on the configured payment allocation strategy (e.g., interest-principal, fee-interest-principal, principal-interest).
- The repayment schedule must be updated accurately after the waiver, reflecting correct values for principal due, interest, fees, penalties, paid amount, in advance amount, late amount, and outstanding balance for each period and in the total row.
- The Loan Transactions tab must display the Interest Payment Waiver transaction with the correct date, amount, and breakdown across principal, interest, fees, and penalties, along with the resulting loan balance.
- The system must generate correct journal entries for the Interest Payment Waiver transaction, debiting the Interest Income account and crediting the appropriate receivable accounts (Loans Receivable and/or Interest/Fee Receivable) based on the allocation.
- If the waiver amount results in an overpayment, the loan status must change to "OVERPAID," the overpaid amount must be tracked, and the corresponding journal entries must include the Overpayment account.
- The system must support undoing an Interest Payment Waiver transaction, reverting the repayment schedule, transaction history, and journal entries to their prior state.
- The system must correctly handle scenarios where a waiver is applied before the due date, followed by a subsequent repayment for the remaining due amount on the due date, ensuring accurate calculation of "in advance," "late," and "outstanding" values.

As a Loan Officer,
I want to define interest pause periods on a loan's repayment schedule so that interest does not accrue during the specified pause window,
So that customers are not charged interest for periods where repayment obligations are temporarily suspended, while the loan schedule automatically recalculates to reflect the adjusted interest and outstanding balances.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When an interest pause period is created with a start and end date, the system triggers a LoanScheduleVariationsAddedBusinessEvent reflecting the specified pause range, and a LoanBalanceChangedBusinessEvent is raised on the appropriate transaction date.
- The repayment schedule must recalculate interest for all outstanding periods affected by the pause, reducing the interest due for the paused days while adjusting principal, balance, due, and outstanding amounts accordingly, without altering already paid installments.
- The system must support creating an interest pause period within the same period as an unpaid installment, between multiple future periods, retroactively (backdated) after a repayment has already been made, and support multiple overlapping or sequential pause periods within the same loan, with each new pause correctly recalculating the schedule and marking affected transactions as replayed where applicable.
- After applying one or more interest pauses, the loan must still be payable in full, and performing a pay-off transaction on any given date must close the loan with zero outstanding balance and all installments marked as having their obligations met.

As a Finance Manager,
I want the Transaction Summary Reports (including the version with Asset Owner details) to accurately capture and display all buydown fee related transaction types—such as Buy Down Fee, Buy Down Fee Amortization, Buy Down Fee Adjustment, and Buy Down Fee Amortization Adjustment—along with their correct allocation across Fees, Interest, Penalty, Principal, and Unallocated Credit categories,
So that I can reliably reconcile loan transactions and verify the correct accounting treatment of buydown fees regardless of whether they are configured as an income type of "FEE" or another allocation type.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a loan is disbursed and a buydown fee transaction is recorded, the Transaction Summary Report for that date must correctly reflect the Disbursement and Buy Down Fee transaction amounts, allocating the fee amount to the appropriate category (Interest or Fees) based on the product's configured buydown fee income type.
- After running the COB (Close of Business) job on a subsequent date, the Transaction Summary Report must include a "Buy Down Fee Amortization" entry with the correctly calculated periodic amortization amount allocated to the appropriate category (Interest or Fees) consistent with the product configuration.
- When a buydown fee adjustment (both a direct adjustment and an adjustment referencing an original buydown fee transaction) is applied, the Transaction Summary Report must show both a "Buy Down Fee Adjustment" entry and a corresponding "Buy Down Fee Amortization Adjustment" entry, with negative transaction amounts correctly reflecting the reduction, allocated to the appropriate category (Interest or Fees).
- The Transaction Summary Report with Asset Owner must mirror all the same transaction entries, dates, types, payment types, and amounts as the standard Transaction Summary Report, additionally exposing Asset Owner ID and From Asset Owner ID columns for reporting purposes.
- All reported transaction amounts must remain consistent whether the loan product's buydown fee income type is configured as default (Interest allocation) or explicitly as "FEE" (Fees allocation), with amounts correctly routed to the corresponding column in each case.

As a Loan Administrator,
I want to configure and apply disbursement charges on interest-bearing progressive loans using different calculation types (Flat amount, Percentage of Amount, and Percentage of Loan Amount plus Interest),
So that I can accurately charge fees at disbursement time and ensure correct accounting, repayment schedules, and loan balances are maintained throughout the loan lifecycle.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a disbursement charge is configured with a "Flat" calculation type and a specified amount, the system must display the correct due charge amount on the Loan Charges tab, deduct it from the disbursement transaction as a "Repayment (at time of disbursement)" entry, and post the corresponding Fee Income and Suspense/Clearing account journal entries.
- When a disbursement charge is configured with a "Percentage of Amount" calculation type, the system must calculate the charge based on the specified percentage of the transaction amount and reflect it consistently across the Loan Charges tab, Repayment Schedule, Loan Transactions tab, and Journal Entries.
- When a disbursement charge is configured with a "Percentage of Loan Amount + Interest" calculation type, the system must calculate the charge based on both principal and total interest, and this value must be reflected consistently across the Loan Charges tab, Repayment Schedule, Loan Transactions tab, and Journal Entries.
- Regardless of the calculation type, the disbursement charge must be fully paid off immediately upon disbursement, with the Loan Charges tab reflecting zero Outstanding and full Paid amount right after disbursement.
- Regular repayments made after disbursement must correctly reduce the outstanding principal and interest balances according to the repayment schedule, without being affected by the disbursement charge once it has been settled.
- Upon full repayment (via Pay-off) of the outstanding principal and interest, the loan must be closed with a zero outstanding balance, and all installments must have their obligations marked as met.

As an Admin,
I want to enable, configure, and manage the business date within the system,
So that I can control and maintain accurate date-based operations either manually or through scheduled automation.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The system allows enabling or disabling the "enable-business-date" global configuration.
- The Admin can manually set the business date to a specific value and verify it is correctly applied.
- The Admin can update the business date multiple times, with each change being correctly reflected.
- The system supports incrementing the business date automatically through a scheduled job (e.g., Increase Business Date by 1 day).
- The system validates business date input and returns an appropriate error message when the value is empty or null.
- The system validates business date input and returns an appropriate error message when the value has an invalid or incorrectly formatted date.

As a Loan Administrator,
I want to apply and manage Discount Fee Adjustments on Working Capital Loan accounts,
So that I can accurately correct or reduce previously applied discount fees while maintaining reliable loan balances, transaction history, and accounting records.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Admin can successfully add a Discount Fee Adjustment to an active Working Capital Loan for an amount less than or equal to the remaining discount fee balance, updating the loan's totals (discount, totalDiscountFee, totalDiscountFeeAdjustment) and creating a corresponding "Discount Fee Adjustment" transaction.
- The system rejects Discount Fee Adjustment attempts when the adjustment amount exceeds the available discount fee amount (single or cumulative), when the amount is zero or negative, when the transaction date precedes the related discount fee date, when the transaction date is in the future, or when the loan is not in an Active status (e.g., closed or overpaid), preserving the existing transaction history unchanged in each failure case.
- Multiple Discount Fee Adjustments can be applied successfully on the same date or different dates, correctly appending each adjustment transaction, raising the appropriate WorkingCapitalLoanDiscountFeeAdjustmentTransactionBusinessEvent with correct amount and date, and generating accurate journal entries (debiting Deferred Interest Revenue and crediting Loans Receivable) for each adjustment made.

As a Loan Administrator,
I want to re-age interest-bearing loans using equal amortization interest handling methods and reverse those re-aging transactions when necessary,
So that I can accurately adjust repayment schedules for customers while ensuring the loan can be correctly restored to its original state and still reach full repayment if the re-aging is undone.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a re-aging transaction is applied with a specified interest handling method (e.g., EQUAL_AMORTIZATION_PAYABLE_INTEREST or EQUAL_AMORTIZATION_FULL_INTEREST), the system must recalculate the repayment schedule, splitting the original installment where re-aging starts and generating new installments with recalculated principal and interest amounts based on the outstanding balance.
- The system must correctly record the re-age transaction in the Loan Transactions tab, including the appropriate principal, interest, and outstanding loan balance, without altering previously paid installments.
- When a re-aging transaction is undone, the system must restore the original repayment schedule (matching the state prior to re-aging) and mark the re-age transaction as reverted, while preserving all previous repayment history.
- After undoing a re-aging transaction, the loan must remain payable in full, allowing a pay-off transaction to close the loan with zero outstanding balance and all installments marked as having obligations met.

# User Story

As a Loan Officer,
I want the loan repayment schedule to accurately recalculate principal, interest, fees, and penalties based on different interest recalculation frequencies, payment strategies, partial/late payments, multi-disbursements, and charges added mid-cycle,
So that I can ensure accurate tracking of outstanding balances, due amounts, and payment allocations for customers under various loan repayment scenarios.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given a loan with Declining Balance interest type and interest recalculation frequency set to "Same as Repayment Period", when a customer makes a partial or late repayment, the system must correctly recalculate the remaining periods' principal, interest, due, paid, in advance, late, and outstanding amounts.
- Given a loan with multiple disbursements, when each disbursement occurs at a different date, the system must recalculate the outstanding loan balance and future installment breakdown (principal and interest) accordingly.
- Given a loan configured with the "Due-Penalty-Fee-Interest-Principal-In Advance-Principal-Penalty-Fee-Interest" payment strategy, when a penalty charge with a future due date is added and repayments are made before, on, or after the charge due date, the system must allocate payments in the correct order (due amounts first, then in-advance principal, then remaining penalty/fee/interest) and update the loan transactions, charges, and repayment schedule tabs accurately.
- Given a repayment that fully covers the due installment plus additional charges, when the payment is processed, the system must generate correct transaction records (including accrual entries when applicable) and mark the installment as fully paid with zero outstanding balance.
- In all scenarios, the Loan Repayment Schedule and Total Row must display accurate values for Principal Due, Interest, Fees, Penalties, Due, Paid, In Advance, Late, and Outstanding amounts consistent with the loan’s configured terms and repayment strategy.

As a Loan Officer/Administrator,
I want the loan management system to accurately track overdue status, repayment history, and support various transaction types (refunds, chargebacks, fraud flags) throughout the loan lifecycle,
So that I can ensure correct delinquency reporting, accurate outstanding balances, and proper handling of financial adjustments for compliance and customer service purposes.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a Payout Refund or Merchant Issued Refund transaction fully covers the outstanding balance, the delinquency range must reset to "NO_DELINQUENCY", the delinquent date must be cleared, the loan status must change to "CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET", and the outstanding amount must become zero.
- The system must correctly calculate and report the delinquent date based on the earliest overdue installment, whether a single repayment or multiple repayments are overdue, reflecting the appropriate delinquency range (e.g., RANGE_3, RANGE_30).
- The loan details endpoint must always return the correct "last payment amount/date" and "last repayment amount/date" fields, updating appropriately after each repayment, goodwill credit, transaction reversal, loan closure, or overpayment event.
- Both closed ("CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET") and overpaid ("OVERPAID") loans must be eligible to be flagged as Fraud by an Administrator.
- The repayment schedule must recalculate principal, fees, and outstanding balances correctly when multiple disbursements occur on a loan that already has fees applied.
- When a chargeback transaction is applied after a Goodwill Credit, Payout Refund, or Merchant Issued Refund, the system must reverse the credit correctly, restoring the original due amounts, balances, and reflecting the chargeback in the loan transaction history.

As a Loan Administrator,
I want to associate one or more loan originators with a Working Capital loan, either inline at submission time or afterward via attach/detach APIs,
So that I can accurately track which originator(s) referred or managed each Working Capital loan throughout its lifecycle while ensuring only valid, active originators are linked.

Acceptance Criteria:
- An originator attached to a Working Capital loan before approval must remain attached and visible in the loan details throughout submission, approval, undo-approval, re-approval, and disbursement.
- A loan can be created with one or more originators attached inline at submission time, either by referencing an existing originator's external ID, by referencing multiple distinct originators, or by creating a new originator on the fly (when enabled by configuration); duplicate inline references to the same originator must result in only a single attachment.
- Originators can be attached to or detached from a loan by internal ID, by originator external ID, by loan external ID, or by both external IDs, and the full originator record (including all fields) must be retrievable through the loan details and dedicated originators endpoints.
- Attaching an inactive/pending originator, attaching a duplicate originator, or modifying originators on an already-approved loan must be rejected with a 403 status, while operations referencing non-existent originators or non-existent loans must be rejected with a 404 status, including rollback of loan creation when an inline originator reference is invalid.

As a Loan Officer,
I want the system to automatically recalculate interest on the outstanding repayment schedule when installments become overdue, whether fully unpaid or partially paid late,
So that the loan balance, interest accrual, and future installment amounts remain accurate and reflect the actual repayment behavior of the customer.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a loan is disbursed with an interest recalculation strategy (such as "till rest frequency date" or "till preclose") and daily interest calculation, the initial repayment schedule must correctly reflect principal, interest, fees, penalties, and outstanding balances for all periods.
- When the first installment is paid in full on its due date, the repayment schedule and transaction history must correctly mark that period as fully paid with zero outstanding balance, without affecting future installments.
- When a subsequent installment becomes overdue (fully unpaid) and the business date passes the due date, running the COB job must trigger interest recalculation and an accrual transaction, updating the remaining installments' principal, interest, and outstanding amounts accordingly, while preserving the total loan balance consistency in the Total row.
- When a subsequent installment is partially paid after its due date (late payment), the system must correctly split the payment between "Paid" and "Late" amounts for that period, and recalculate interest for the remaining unpaid periods based on the selected recalculation frequency (daily or till rest frequency date).
- After any overdue or partial late payment event, subsequent COB job execution must recalculate interest accurately according to the configured recalculation strategy, ensuring that the Loan Repayment Schedule Total row and the Loan Transactions tab consistently reflect updated principal, interest, due, paid, in advance, late, and outstanding values.

As a Loan Officer,
I want the system to correctly calculate and manage progressive loan repayment schedules, disbursements, chargebacks, and pay-offs—including edge cases with very small disbursement amounts and various future installment allocation strategies (NEXT_INSTALLMENT, LAST_INSTALLMENT)—under the Advanced Payment Allocation strategy,
So that loan balances, repayment schedules, and transaction records remain accurate and consistent, and improper actions (such as undoing a transaction linked to a chargeback) are correctly blocked with clear error messages.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a progressive loan is created with a very small total disbursement amount (e.g., less than 1 unit) and disbursed partially, the repayment schedule and loan transactions must accurately reflect the disbursed amount, and a full pay-off must close the loan with zero outstanding balance and all installment obligations met, regardless of whether the loan has 1 or multiple repayment periods.
- When a repayment transaction has a linked chargeback, attempting to undo that repayment transaction must be rejected with a 403 error and the message "update not allowed as loan transaction is linked to other transactions"; the loan must still be payable off and closed with zero outstanding balance afterward.
- When the loan product's future installment allocation rule is set to NEXT_INSTALLMENT for vertical progressive loan schedules, a full prepayment made before the term ends must correctly reallocate paid amounts across all remaining installments (marking them as paid in advance where applicable), generate the appropriate accrual transaction, and close the loan with zero outstanding balance.
- When the loan product's future installment allocation rule is set to LAST_INSTALLMENT for vertical progressive loan schedules, the system must calculate and apply the repayment schedule, disbursement, and prepayment behavior consistently with the defined allocation rule, ensuring accurate totals for principal, interest, fees, penalties, due, paid, in-advance, late, and outstanding amounts across all periods.

As a loan officer,
I want to terminate a progressive loan contract with automatic interest recalculation at any point in its lifecycle,
So that I can accurately close out loans early while ensuring the outstanding balance, interest, and repayment schedule are correctly recalculated as of the termination date.

Acceptance Criteria:
- When a contract termination is performed on an installment due date, the system recalculates the repayment schedule to show only the periods up to and including the termination date, with interest accrued and due amounts correctly adjusted, and generates matching Accrual and Contract Termination transactions.
- When a contract termination is performed before an installment date (e.g., mid-period), the system prorates the interest calculation up to the termination date, updates the schedule and total row accordingly, and records the correct Accrual and Contract Termination transactions with zero remaining outstanding balance.
- When a contract termination is performed in the middle of an installment period, the system recalculates the number of days, interest due, and outstanding balance up to that exact date, ensuring the transactions tab reflects accurate Accrual and Contract Termination entries.
- When a contract termination is performed after the loan's maturity date (with prior repayments already made and the "is-principal-compounding-disabled-for-overdue-loans" configuration enabled), the system correctly recalculates the remaining schedule, interest, and balances based on payments already applied.
- After any successful contract termination and subsequent loan pay-off on the same date, the loan must be closed with a zero outstanding balance, and all installments must show that their obligations have been fully met.

As a system integrator managing loan operations,
I want to perform Working Capital Loan operations (create, modify, approve, disburse, reject, withdraw, add discount fee, and fetch details/transactions) through a single Batch API, referencing loans by either internal ID or external ID, and optionally chaining multiple steps within one enclosing transaction,
So that I can efficiently automate and orchestrate complete Working Capital Loan lifecycles in a single request while ensuring data consistency and proper rollback when any step fails.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The Batch API must support individual operations on Working Capital Loans, including creation, modification, approval, disbursement, rejection, withdrawal/deletion, discount fee addition, and fetching loan details or transactions, all returning a 200OK response and correctly updated loan data upon success.
- The Batch API must support referencing a Working Capital Loan by either its internal loan ID or its external ID for all supported operations, with equivalent behavior and correct data returned in both cases.
- The Batch API must support executing multiple chained Working Capital Loan steps (e.g., create, approve, disburse, add discount fee, fetch details) within a single call, correctly reflecting the final loan status and all resulting transactions.
- When enclosingTransaction is set to "true" and any step in the chain fails, all previously executed steps within that batch call must be rolled back, and the failing step must return an error with code 400.
- When enclosingTransaction is set to "false", each step in the chain must be evaluated independently, allowing prior successful steps to persist even if a later step fails, with each step's individual result status (200 or error code) verifiable.

As a Loan Officer,
I want to generate and retrieve a projected amortization schedule for a working capital loan,
So that I can review the expected payment breakdown, balances, and discount fee allocation over the life of the loan before disbursement.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Given a client with an approved working capital loan, the system must allow an admin to generate a projected amortization schedule by providing the discount fee amount, net disbursement amount, total payment volume, period payment rate, NPV day count, and expected disbursement date.
- The retrieved amortization schedule must return accurate summary fields, including discount fee amount, net disbursement amount, total payment volume, period payment rate, NPV day count, expected payment amount, and the original number of payments.
- The retrieved amortization schedule must return a detailed list of payments, each including payment number, date, expected payment amount, expected balance, expected amortization amount, and expected discount fee balance, calculated correctly for every installment from disbursement through full repayment.

As a system administrator,
I want to validate currency configuration updates and reject invalid values,
So that the system maintains valid configuration data and prevents incorrect currency settings.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Updating currency with an empty value must return an error.
- Updating currency with a NULL value must return an error.
- Updating currency with an invalid string value must return an error.
- Updating currency with the literal value "null" must return an error.

As a finance product administrator,
I want to create, update, retrieve, list, and delete Working Capital Loan Products with full validation of their configuration,
So that I can define compliant loan products with correct delinquency, accounting, breach, and payment allocation settings.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Admin can create, update, delete, and verify deletion of a Working Capital Loan Product using its normal identifier.
- Admin can create, update, delete, and verify deletion of a Working Capital Loan Product using its external-id.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when mandatory fields are missing or null, including name, shortName, currencyCode, digitsAfterDecimal, amortizationType, npvDayCount, principal, periodPaymentRate, and repaymentFrequencyType.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when fields exceed maximum allowed lengths for name, shortName, description, and currencyCode.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when fields exceed maximum allowed lengths for name, shortName, description, and currencyCode.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when zero values are supplied for npvDayCount, principal, minPrincipal, maxPrincipal, or delinquencyBucketId.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when zero values are supplied for npvDayCount, principal, minPrincipal, maxPrincipal, or delinquencyBucketId.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails with validation errors for invalid values of digitsAfterDecimal, inMultiplesOf, discount, principal, periodPaymentRate, and locale.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails with validation errors for invalid values of digitsAfterDecimal, inMultiplesOf, discount, principal, periodPaymentRate, and locale.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when payment allocation rules are invalid in count, values, or missing the DEFAULT transaction type.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when payment allocation rules are invalid in count or values.
- Deleting a Working Capital Loan Product fails when the product id does not exist.
- Retrieving a Working Capital Loan Product fails when the product id does not exist.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be created with delinquencyGraceDays and delinquencyStartType set to LOAN_CREATION or DISBURSEMENT.
- A Working Capital Loan Product created without delinquencyGraceDays defaults delinquencyGraceDays and delinquencyStartType to null.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be updated to set delinquencyGraceDays and delinquencyStartType.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be updated to change delinquencyGraceDays and delinquencyStartType.
- The Working Capital Loan Product template exposes delinquencyStartType options LOAN_CREATION and DISBURSEMENT.
- Creating or updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when delinquencyGraceDays is negative or delinquencyStartType is invalid.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be created with breachId.
- Creating or updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when breachId is invalid or does not exist.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be created with accounting rule ACC_DEF_REV_AM and the rule is persisted correctly.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be created with accounting rule NONE and has no accounting mappings.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product with ACC_DEF_REV_AM fails when required GL accounts are missing.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product with ACC_DEF_REV_AM fails when a GL account id does not exist.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when the GL account type for loanPortfolio is incorrect.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product can change accounting rule from NONE to ACC_DEF_REV_AM and from ACC_DEF_REV_AM to NONE.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product with ACC_DEF_REV_AM can update GL account mappings, including a single mapping such as writeOff.
- Deleting a Working Capital Loan Product created with accounting mappings cleans up the associated GL account mappings.
- The Working Capital Loan Product list includes the accounting rule field for created products.
- The Working Capital Loan Product template exposes accounting options, including NONE and ACC_DEF_REV_AM.
- A Working Capital Loan Product can be created and updated with breach and near breach values when breach frequency is valid and not lower than near breach frequency.
- Creating or updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when breach frequency is lower than near breach frequency.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when near breach is specified without breach.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when near breach is specified without breach.
- Creating or updating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when near breach fields contain invalid values such as an invalid nearBreachId.
- The Working Capital Loan Product template exposes the six advanced payment allocation types: DUE_PENALTY, DUE_FEE, DUE_PRINCIPAL, IN_ADVANCE_PENALTY, IN_ADVANCE_FEE, and IN_ADVANCE_PRINCIPAL.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product persists the payment allocation order exactly as submitted.
- Updating a Working Capital Loan Product changes the payment allocation order exactly as submitted.
- Creating a Working Capital Loan Product fails when payment allocation rules contain duplicates.

As a loan operations manager,
I want the loan delinquency and next-payment calculations to correctly reflect repayments, payoffs, refunds, chargebacks, pauses, and COB recalculations,
So that overdue status, next due amount, and delinquency dates are accurate for progressive loans with daily interest recalculation.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The system must calculate the loan repayment schedule for a progressive loan with daily interest recalculation and advanced payment allocation.
- The system must set the initial loan-level next payment due date and next payment amount correctly after disbursement.
- When an overpayment is made before the first installment, the repayment schedule must be recalculated and the loan-level next payment amount must reflect the remaining amount due on the next unpaid installment.
- After COB runs on later dates, the repayment schedule and next payment amount must remain consistent with the recalculated schedule.
- When a payoff is made after an overpayment scenario, all installments must be marked as obligations met.
- When the loan reaches the last installment, the loan-level next payment amount must reflect the remaining amount due on the last installment.
- When a repayment is made before the last installment, the system must recalculate the remaining installments and update the next payment amount accordingly.
- When the future installment allocation rule is set to LAST_INSTALLMENT, a payoff must allocate the remaining amount to the last installment as expected.
- When the future installment allocation rule is set to NEXT_INSTALLMENT, a payoff must allocate the remaining amount to the next installment as expected.
- When a payoff is made on the first installment, the system must close the loan and mark all installments as obligations met.
- When a loan has a down payment, the repayment schedule must include the down payment installment and the loan-level next payment amount must reflect the first scheduled installment.
- When a merchant-issued refund is posted, the system must create the refund and interest refund transactions and recalculate the repayment schedule accordingly.
- After a refund and subsequent COB run, the loan-level next payment amount must reflect the updated outstanding installment amount.
- When a payoff is made after a refund scenario, all installments must be marked as obligations met.
- The system must support delinquency pause periods and exclude paused days from installment-level delinquency calculations.
- The system must calculate loan delinquent days correctly when graceOnArrearsAgeing is configured at the loan product level.
- The system must override graceOnArrearsAgeing at the loan level when provided and use the loan-level value for delinquency calculations.
- The system must return the correct pastDueDate for an overdue loan.
- The system must return a null pastDueDate when the loan is not overdue.
- When a chargeback creates overdue, the system must set pastDueDate to the chargeback date.
- The LoanBalanceChangedBusinessEvent must include the correct pastDueDate for overdue loans.
- The LoanBalanceChangedBusinessEvent must include a null pastDueDate when the loan is not overdue.
- When a chargeback creates overdue, the LoanBalanceChangedBusinessEvent must include the chargeback date as pastDueDate.

As a loan operations user,
I want to re-age delinquent loans and have the repayment schedule, transactions, delinquency status, and related events updated correctly,
So that overdue loans can be restructured accurately while preserving accounting integrity and supporting payoff, undo, chargeback, and replay scenarios.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A loan re-aging transaction can be created successfully for a delinquent loan using a specified start date, frequency, frequency type, and number of installments.
- Creating a re-aging transaction recalculates the repayment schedule into the expected number of periods and updates principal due, due amounts, outstanding amounts, paid amounts, and installment dates correctly.
- Re-aging can be performed on loans with advanced payment allocation and produces the correct repayment schedule for the chosen loan product and payment strategy.
- Re-aging can be created using the loan external ID as well as directly on the loan.
- Re-aging updates the loan transactions tab with a Re-age transaction showing the correct amount, principal allocation, loan balance, and reverted status.
- Re-aging clears delinquency for the loan when appropriate and updates delinquency range and delinquent date correctly.
- Inline COB processing updates delinquency range before re-aging and reflects the correct delinquency state afterward.
- A loan re-aging transaction can be undone, restoring the prior repayment schedule and transaction state.
- Undoing a re-aging transaction restores delinquency status to the pre-re-age state.
- Re-aging can be replayed after undoing, and the loan transactions tab reflects reverted and replayed states correctly.
- Re-aging works correctly when there are prior repayments, including autopay repayments and backdated repayments.
- Re-aging works correctly when there are prior chargebacks, including chargebacks before maturity and after maturity.
- Re-aging works correctly when there are charge adjustments or NSF fees added before or after the re-aging date.
- Re-aging works correctly when there are backdated disbursements or additional disbursements before or after the re-aging date.
- Re-aging works correctly when there is a merchant issued refund before re-aging.
- Re-aging works correctly when there are multiple disbursements on the loan, including second disbursements before or after the re-aging date.
- Re-aging can merge or remove normal installments as required when the re-aging start date falls before maturity, on maturity, or within an installment bucket.
- Re-aging can create additional installments when the re-aging start date and frequency require them, including N+1 installment scenarios.
- Re-aging can be previewed before creation, and the preview shows the expected repayment schedule without committing the transaction.
- The re-aging preview and the committed re-aging transaction produce consistent repayment schedule totals.
- Loan payoff after re-aging closes the loan with zero outstanding balance and all installment obligations met.
- Loan payoff after undoing or replaying re-aging still closes the loan correctly.

- When a partially paid loan is reopened by undoing a repayment, the loan status shall return to `ACTIVE` and the repayment schedule shall be recalculated with the correct outstanding amount.

- When a backdated charge is added after a repayment, the repayment schedule shall reflect the charge allocation and any resulting accrual activity adjustments.

- When a disbursement is later undone, the repayment schedule and accrual transactions shall be recalculated accordingly.

- The system shall support loans with interest recognition on disbursement date and include disbursement-day interest in accrual calculations.

- When `charge-accrual-date` is set to `submitted-date`, accruals for charges on closed or overpaid loans shall be recognized based on the loan submitted date.
- For closed or overpaid loans, accrual activity shall still be posted correctly for charge accruals according to the configured accrual date.
- For closed or overpaid loans, repayment after accrual activity shall update the repayment schedule and transaction history without creating negative accrual activity amounts.
- For loans with interest recognition on disbursement date, early repayments shall recalculate future interest and repayment amounts correctly.
- For loans with interest recognition on disbursement date, repayments on the disbursement date shall allocate principal immediately and accrue no interest for that day.
- For loans with interest recognition on disbursement date, repayments on installment dates shall still produce correct accrual activity and repayment schedule totals.
- For loans with interest recognition on disbursement date, the system shall calculate fractional-period interest correctly for partial periods.
- When a repayment is made and later undone, the system shall preserve transaction external IDs for accrual activity transactions that were reverse-replayed.
- When an accrual activity transaction is reversed and replayed, the replayed transaction shall retain the original external ID.

- When an interest payment waiver is applied after accrual activity exists, the repayment schedule shall be recalculated without reversing the waiver transaction.
- When a loan is fully repaid, the loan status shall become `CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET` and outstanding amount shall become zero.
- When a loan is overpaid, the loan status shall become `OVERPAID` and the overpaid amount shall be tracked.

As a loan officer,

- A second disbursement mid-period must recalculate the schedule correctly, including the impact on the next installment and total outstanding amounts.
- A second disbursement before the first repayment date must not extend the term count incorrectly and must recalculate future installments based on the new balance.

- Early repayments must be applied as advance payments and reduce future installment obligations according to advanced payment allocation rules.
- Merchant-issued refunds must be treated as repayment-like allocations and update the schedule and transaction tab accordingly.
- Down payment transactions must reduce principal immediately, update active term count, and be reflected in both schedule and transaction history.
- Auto down payments must be recorded as down payment transactions and affect the schedule the same way as manual down payments.

- Undoing the last disbursement must revert the schedule back to the prior state and remove the effect of the latest disbursement transaction.
- Re-aging a loan must create a re-age transaction, extend or restructure the schedule as configured, and preserve prior paid installments.
- Re-aging with different interest handling modes must recalculate future installments and totals according to the selected handling rule.
- Interest pause periods must reduce or eliminate interest accrual during the paused dates and recalculate affected installments.
- Backdated repayments must trigger reverse-replay behavior and recalculate the schedule from the backdated payment date forward.
- Backdated charges must trigger reverse-replay behavior and update repayment allocations, schedule totals, and transaction replay flags.
- Chargebacks must reverse prior repayment allocations, restore balances, and recalculate the schedule correctly.
- Charge-off must create accrual and charge-off transactions, update the schedule, and allow payoff of the remaining balance.
- Charge-off with zero-interest behavior must close the loan without accruing additional interest at charge-off.
- Contract termination must close the loan and move the remaining balance into a termination transaction with the correct accrued interest.
- Re-amortization must recalculate the remaining schedule from the re-amortization date using the configured interest handling rule.
- Rescheduling must adjust due dates, optionally add extra terms, and recalculate installment amounts and totals from the reschedule date.
- Payment holidays must shift due dates and recalculate the schedule correctly after the holiday period.
- Charges due before or between disbursements must appear in the schedule and charges tab with correct due, paid, waived, and outstanding amounts.
- Waiving a charge must reduce outstanding charge amounts, update the repayment schedule, and record a waive transaction.
- Undoing a waived charge must restore the charge outstanding amount and revert the waive transaction.
- Due date charges added before or after disbursements must be allocated to the correct installment or final installment depending on maturity rules.
- Snooze fees and NSF fees must be reflected in the repayment schedule and charges tab with correct fee and penalty allocation.
- Multiple charges after maturity must be grouped and allocated correctly across the final installment or N+1 installment as configured.
- Capitalized income transactions must increase loan balance, create capitalized income transactions, and recalculate future installments.
- Chargeback after maturity must still reverse the original repayment and preserve correct outstanding balances.
- Write-off must close the loan as written off and create the correct close transaction with principal and interest components.
- Loan status must reflect closed written-off state after write-off.
- Loan balance changed business events and schedule variation events must be created when applicable.
- Loan transactions tab must accurately reflect all disbursements, repayments, refunds, chargebacks, accruals, waives, re-ages, re-amortizations, terminations, charge-offs, and closures with correct amounts and replay/revert flags.

As a loan administrator,

- A loan cannot be created when the submitted date is after the business date.

As a loan operations user,
I want to recalculate repayment schedules when a loan interest rate is changed backdated or mid-loan,
So that repayments, accruals, charge-offs, payoffs, refunds, and closures remain accurate across all loan lifecycle events.

- The system must generate an initial repayment schedule for a newly disbursed loan using the configured interest rate, repayment frequency, and allocation rules.

- When the interest rate change is submitted on an installment due date, the schedule must correctly handle the due installment and any subsequent installments.
- When the interest rate change is submitted in the middle of an installment period, the schedule must recalculate interest proportionally from the effective date.
- When a repayment is reversed/undone after an interest rate change, the repayment schedule and transaction history must be replayed and updated consistently.
- When a repayment is reversed/undone before any interest rate change has occurred, the schedule must be recalculated from the reversal date and reflect the restored outstanding balance.
- When a loan is paid off after a backdated interest rate change, all installments must be marked as obligations met and the loan must close correctly.
- When a loan is charged off after a backdated interest rate change, the charge-off amount must include the correct principal, accrued interest, and any applicable adjustments.
- When a charged-off loan has a backdated interest rate change approved, the repayment schedule must be rebuilt to reflect the new interest rate and the charge-off transaction must be replayed accordingly.
- When a charged-off loan is later paid off, the loan must close with obligations met and zero outstanding balance.
- When a loan is written off and then a backdated interest rate change is approved, the written-off close transaction must be replayed with the correct recalculated amount.
- When a loan has an external asset owner and a backdated interest rate change is approved, the asset externalization details must remain consistent and reflect the correct effective dates and status transitions.
- When a loan has a zero-interest product and a backdated interest rate change is approved, the schedule must recalculate interest from zero to the new rate and update totals accordingly.
- When a loan has a backdated interest rate change and a credit balance refund is applied, the loan must move from overpaid to closed with obligations met once the excess is refunded.
- When a loan is already closed with obligations met, a backdated interest rate change must still recalculate the schedule correctly without reopening the loan.
- When a loan is overpaid and then a backdated interest rate change is approved, the system must preserve the overpaid amount and loan status until any required refund is processed.
- When a loan product defines minimum and maximum allowed interest rates, rescheduling with a new interest rate outside those bounds must fail with a validation error.
- When a loan product allows a minimal positive interest rate, rescheduling must succeed and calculate interest using the minimum allowed rate.
- When a loan uses weekly repayments, backdated interest rate changes must recalculate weekly installment amounts and interest correctly.
- When a loan has a merchant-issued refund or credit balance refund after a backdated interest rate change, the repayment schedule must update paid, in-advance, late, and outstanding amounts correctly.
- When a repayment is reversed after a merchant-issued refund and backdated interest change, the schedule must rebuild overdue balances and interest correctly.
- When a loan has overdue installments and COB runs after a backdated interest rate change, overdue balance correction amounts must be recalculated correctly.
- When COB runs after a reversal on a loan with overdue installments, overdue balance correction amounts must be rebuilt for all overdue periods.

As a loan operations admin,

As a loan administrator,

As a loan administrator,

As a admin,
I want to process repayment chargebacks on loans and have the loan balance, status, and delinquency/overdue treatment updated correctly,
So that reversed or adjusted repayments are reflected accurately in loan servicing and collections.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A chargeback of type `REPAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_CHARGEBACK` on a closed loan reopens the loan and restores the charged-back amount as outstanding.
- A chargeback of type `REPAYMENT_ADJUSTMENT_REFUND` on a closed loan reopens the loan and restores the refunded amount as outstanding.
- If a loan is fully repaid and closed, a later chargeback makes the loan active again with the chargeback amount outstanding.
- If a loan becomes active again after a chargeback, a subsequent repayment can close the loan again when the outstanding amount is fully paid.
- A second chargeback after the loan has been repaid again reopens the loan and sets the new outstanding amount accordingly.
- If an NSF fee is added after a repayment undo and the loan is repaid again, a later chargeback still reopens the loan and restores the charged-back amount as outstanding.
- If a loan is overpaid and the chargeback amount is greater than the overpaid amount, the loan becomes active with the remaining amount outstanding.
- If a loan is overpaid and the chargeback amount is less than the overpaid amount, the loan remains overpaid and no outstanding amount is created.
- If a loan is overpaid and the chargeback amount exactly matches the overpaid amount, the loan returns to closed obligations met with no outstanding amount.
- Chargebacks must be reflected correctly in delinquency and overdue calculations after COB processing.
- After a chargeback on a partially repaid loan, the delinquency range and delinquent date must be recalculated correctly.
- After a chargeback on a partially repaid loan, total overdue amount must include the reversed repayment amount.

As a product owner,
I want the system to generate and evaluate working capital loan breach schedules based on product breach configuration, loan lifecycle state, disbursement date, and business date,
So that I can monitor repayment risk and identify breach periods accurately for active working capital loans.

Acceptance Criteria:
- No breach schedule is created for a working capital loan that is still in "Submitted and pending approval" state.
- No breach schedule is created for a working capital loan that is only "Approved" and not yet disbursed.
- A breach schedule is created on the disbursement date for an active working capital loan using a breach-enabled product.
- On the last day of the first period, the breach schedule remains unevaluated and does not mark breach.
- On the first day after the first period ends, the first period is evaluated as breached and the next period is generated.
- As business date advances across multiple periods, all completed periods are marked breached and the current open period remains unevaluated.
- The minimum payment amount is calculated correctly when a discount is applied at disbursement.
- A custom breach configuration using 7-day periods, 3 delinquency grace days, and 3 breach grace days generates the expected 10 weekly periods and evaluates breaches according to business date.
- No breach schedule is generated when the loan product does not have breach configuration enabled.
- A custom breach configuration using WEEKS frequency generates a single weekly period on the disbursement day with the expected breach schedule behavior.

As a loan operations administrator,
I want to apply and amortize buy down fees on loans with automated payment allocation,
So that fee income is recognized correctly over time and loan repayment schedules, transactions, and accounting entries remain accurate.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A fully customized loan can be created, approved, and disbursed with the buy down fee-enabled loan product.
- When a buy down fee is added with AUTOPAY payment type, the loan repayment schedule is recalculated to include the fee impact and the expected installment amounts.

- When the business date advances and COB runs, buy down fee amortization transactions must be generated according to the configured amortization behavior.
- Daily amortization must create a buy down fee amortization transaction for each business day with the correct amount.
- Each buy down fee amortization transaction must create the correct journal entries, debiting Deferred Capitalized Income and crediting Income From Buy Down.
- The buy down fee details must be updated as amortization occurs, reducing the not-yet-amortized amount and increasing the amortized amount.
- Repayments made on scheduled dates must allocate amounts correctly between principal and interest while keeping the loan active until fully repaid.
- After all scheduled repayments and required accruals/amortizations are processed, the loan must close with status CLOSED_OBLIGATIONS_MET.
- A LoanBuyDownFeeAmortizationTransactionCreatedBusinessEvent must be published when buy down fee amortization is created.

As a loan officer,
I want repayment transactions on working capital loans to allocate amounts correctly across principal, fees, and penalties according to the configured allocation rule,

Acceptance Criteria:

- The system must support repayment allocation using `DUE_PENALTY_FEE_PRINCIPAL`, applying repayment amounts to due penalty, due fee, then principal.

- The system must support repayment allocation using `IN_ADVANCE_PENALTY_FEE_PRINCIPAL`, applying repayment amounts to advance penalty, advance fee, then principal.

- When a repayment is posted on the charge due date, the repayment transaction must be split into the correct principal, fee, and penalty portions based on the configured allocation rule.

- Fee and penalty charge balances must update correctly after repayment, including outstanding and paid amounts.

- For the `DUE_PRINCIPAL_FEE_PENALTY` allocation, if repayment is made on the charge due date, the repayment must allocate to principal first and then to fee and penalty as applicable.
- For the `DUE_FEE_PENALTY_PRINCIPAL` allocation, if repayment is made on the charge due date, the repayment must allocate to fee and penalty before principal.
- For the `DUE_PENALTY_FEE_PRINCIPAL` allocation, if repayment is made on the charge due date, the repayment must allocate to penalty before fee and principal.
- For the `IN_ADVANCE_PENALTY_FEE_PRINCIPAL` allocation, if repayment is made before the charge due date, the repayment must allocate to penalty and fee in advance before principal.

As a [loan administrator],

As a finance administrator,

As a product owner,
I want to allow credit balance refunds on overpaid working capital loans and enforce the correct validation and status transitions,

- A working capital loan that becomes overpaid after repayment can accept a credit balance refund.

- When payment details are provided for a credit balance refund, they are persisted on the transaction and the transaction exposes the selected payment type.
- Multiple partial credit balance refunds can be applied sequentially, and the loan remains OVERPAID until the total refunded amount equals the overpayment.
- Multiple repayments that exceed the total payable amount accumulate into a single overpayment balance.
- The overpayment amount is tracked accurately and exposed on the loan balance.
- A valid credit balance refund classification code can be used and is persisted on the refund transaction.

As a loan operations manager,
I want discount fees on working capital loans to be recorded and amortized correctly during COB,
So that deferred revenue and income are recognized accurately based on whether a discount exists and whether repayments have been made.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A working capital loan can be created, approved, and disbursed with the expected principal, status, and accounting fields.

- If a repayment exists before COB, COB creates a Discount Fee Amortization transaction for the appropriate amortized amount.
- The Discount Fee Amortization transaction posts journal entries debiting Deferred Interest Revenue and crediting Interest Income.
- The original Discount Fee transaction posts journal entries debiting Loans Receivable and crediting Deferred Interest Revenue.
- If a discount is added after disbursement and a repayment exists, COB updates the loan’s realized income, unrealized income, and total paid principal accordingly.
- If a discount is added after disbursement and no repayment exists, COB does not create any Discount Fee Amortization transaction.
- If a discount is added after disbursement and no repayment exists, COB leaves realized income at 0.0 and keeps the full discount amount as unrealized income.
- If no discount is added to the loan, COB does not create any Discount Fee Amortization transaction.
- If no discount is added to the loan, COB does not change the loan’s principal, realized income, or unrealized income during COB.

As a loan administrator,
I want to add, backdate, partially adjust, and undo discount fee adjustments on working capital loans while preserving repayment and accounting integrity,
So that loan balances, transaction history, and journal entries remain accurate across business dates and COB processing.

Acceptance Criteria:

- When a backdated discount fee adjustment is applied after repayments, the loan account must reflect the correct remaining discount, principal, and total paid principal.

- Undoing a discount fee adjustment must reverse the adjustment transaction in the transaction history.
- A partial discount fee adjustment must be allowed.
- When a partial discount fee adjustment is applied, the remaining discount and principal must be reduced by the adjusted amount.
- A partial discount fee adjustment must be recorded as a transaction on the specified backdated transaction date.
- When a backdated discount fee adjustment is applied after COB has recognized income, the system must post a discount fee amortization adjustment on the current business date for the income already recognized up to the previous COB.
- The amortization adjustment must create the correct journal entries between Interest Income and Deferred Interest Revenue.
- When a full discount fee adjustment is applied after COB has recognized income, the system must post a discount fee amortization adjustment on the next COB date.
- The amortization adjustment for a full discount fee adjustment must create the correct journal entries between Interest Income and Deferred Interest Revenue.
- Undoing a full discount fee adjustment must also reverse the related amortization adjustment.
- After undoing a full discount fee adjustment, the loan account must restore the original discount and principal values while preserving prior repayments.

- Updating a Working Capital Delinquency Bucket fails when `minimumPayment` is less than or equal to 0, with an error stating it must be greater than 0.

As a loan operations administrator,

As a loan officer/admin,

- Undoing a repayment that contributed to overpayment must restore the loan to `ACTIVE` when outstanding balance remains.
- Undoing a repayment after a refund on a closed loan must restore the loan to `ACTIVE` with the correct outstanding amount.
- Single repayment reversals must be supported after a credit balance refund.
- Multiple repayment reversals must be supported after a credit balance refund.
- Reversing only the paid portion of an overpaid repayment must restore the correct outstanding amount and loan status.
- Loan transaction history must retain the original DISBURSEMENT, REPAYMENT, and CREDIT_BALANCE_REFUND entries with their corresponding journal entries.

As a loan administrator,
I want to pause and resume delinquency tracking on working capital loans,
So that delinquency schedules reflect temporary pauses accurately and prevent invalid resume actions.

- A delinquency pause can be created for a working capital loan with a start date and end date.

As a finance operations user,
I want goodwill credit transactions on working capital loans to post the correct general ledger entries and loan status outcomes,
So that loan accounting remains accurate across partial payments, fee and penalty allocations, and overpayment scenarios.

Acceptance Criteria:
- A goodwill credit on a working capital loan posts a debit to Goodwill Expense Account and a credit to Loans Receivable for the transaction amount when the amount is fully applied to principal.
- Multiple goodwill credit transactions on the same day each create their own journal entries with the correct debit and credit amounts.
- Multiple goodwill credit transactions on different days are recorded separately with journal entries dated to each transaction date.
- If a goodwill credit exceeds the outstanding loan balance, the loan status becomes OVERPAID.
- When a goodwill credit exceeds the outstanding loan balance, the excess amount is posted to Other Credit Liability while the outstanding principal is credited only up to the remaining loan balance.
- If a working capital loan has a specified due date fee, a goodwill credit allocates part of the transaction to Fee Charge Off and posts the corresponding credit to Interest/Fee Receivable.
- If a working capital loan has a specified due date penalty, a goodwill credit allocates part of the transaction to Fee Charge Off and posts the corresponding credit to Interest/Fee Receivable.
- If a goodwill credit must cover principal, fees, penalties, and still has remaining excess, the journal entries must allocate amounts in this order: principal to Loans Receivable, fees and penalties to Fee Charge Off and Interest/Fee Receivable, and any remainder to Other Credit Liability.
- A partial goodwill credit that does not exceed the outstanding balance posts only the corresponding debit to Goodwill Expense Account and credit to Loans Receivable.
- A goodwill credit on a closed loan posts the appropriate expense debit and overpayment liability credit according to the remaining unapplied amount.

As a loan operations administrator,
I want the system to evaluate Working Capital loans for near breach conditions alongside breach conditions,
So that I can identify loans that are approaching delinquency and manage them before they fully breach.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The system shall calculate near breach for a Working Capital loan period when the configured near breach evaluation date has passed and the cumulative paid amount is strictly less than the configured near breach threshold amount.
- The system shall not set near breach before the configured near breach evaluation date.

- The system shall keep near breach as true once triggered, even if later repayments reduce or clear the outstanding balance.

- The system shall support near breach evaluation when the breach amount calculation type is FLAT.
- The system shall support near breach evaluation when the breach amount calculation type is PERCENTAGE.

- The system shall still calculate breach independently of near breach, including cases where near breach is null and breach becomes true after the period ends.

As a loan operations user,

As a loan administrator,

- The repayment schedule total row must correctly summarize principal due, interest, fees, penalties, due, paid, in advance, late, and outstanding amounts for each loan scenario.
